In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work presents a dataset for testing the robustness of computer vision systems.
we present ObjectNet, a new large scale real world test set for object detection that is controlled for biases.
we have created a large scale dataset for object detection with controls that show that models do not generalize well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to build large scale datasets with controls and how they are necessary to evaluate the limits of object detectors.
ObjectNet provides an important benchmark for the object detection community.
we are pushing the limits of the field by developing a new dataset that is both harder and easier than existing datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lack of controls in large computer vision benchmarks has resulted in a situation where models are overfit to the training data and do not perform as well in real world scenarios.
the performance of models on benchmarks is often not predictive of real world results.
controls are a powerful tool for creating datasets that push the limits of object detectors and other models.
